In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
medieval exchange rates do indeed include an element of implicit interest, and that this is a significant factor in the calculation of the medieval interest rate.

the relationship between exchange rate movements and the interest rate is not as simple as it is in a modern economy and that there is no simple answer to whether exchange transactions could be used to evade usury prohibitions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

medieval interest rates were high, that they varied considerably across financial centres, that they were generally lower in the 14th century than in the 15th and that there is little evidence of a secular decline in the long run.
the medieval exchange rate data provides us with a rich source of information on interest rates, which can help to fill some of the gaps in our knowledge of medieval finance and the economy.
